gates_glossary.desc: hit ≥ 0.90 on append and tool_turn at 32K and 128K.
needles at 10/50/90 correct at 32K and 128K; a truncated answer (reasoning > 4096 tokens) does not count as a failure.
swap delta ≤ 0.5 GB in every band.
zero HTTP 4xx/5xx errors or stream errors at 32K and 128K.
a peak above 102 GB raises a warning and does not eliminate: it is the normal operating point of mlx-serve.

scenarios.eval: Full prompt with no cache. Measures the first turn (cold TTFT) and prefill; primes the cache.
Same prompt again. Best synthetic case for reuse.
Previous prompt + new suffix. A conversation turn.
Edit in the middle of the prompt. Expected reuse is ~half; excluded from T_turn.
Previous prompt + tool result. An agent turn; included in T_turn.

correctness.eval: Needles at 10%, 50% and 90% of the fixture. Correct = all three in the answer.

test_catalog.t_turno: T_turn = tool_turn TTFT + 512 / median decode of the served warm scenarios (identical, append, tool_turn). It is the wait for one agent turn with a 512-token reply. Lower is better.

Abliterated pack, same config.json as c1. T_turn within 1% at 32K/128K, MTP acceptance 0.58, zero stream failures. Refuses 0/50 legitimate prompts, same as c1 — no over-refusal to fix. But on 24 harmful prompts a safe model should refuse, c1 refuses 7/24 and u1 refuses 0/24: abliteration removed the base's residual safety. Viable on responsiveness, less safe as a default.

takeaways: c1 goes from 11.0 s at 32K to 12.35 s at 128K, 13.9 s at 256K and 13.6 s at 512K; c3 from 13.5 to 17.7 s; c2 from 17.1 to 27.3 s (3 reps, Stage C at 256K/512K).
at 128K c1 and c3 both decode ~50 tok/s; the warm turn responds in 2.1 s on c1 and 4.8 s on c3. At 256K the tool turn is 2.2 s on c1 vs 5.8 s on c3.

u1 (abliterated, same runtime and quant) lands T_turn within 1% of c1 at 32K and 128K, MTP acceptance 0.58, zero stream failures. Both c1 and u1 refuse 0/50 legitimate prompts.

On 24 harmful prompts a safe model should refuse, c1 refuses 7/24 and u1 refuses 0/24. Abliteration stripped the base's residual safety, so u1 is not an upgrade — it is measurably less safe as a default. (c1 itself is permissive: it answers 17/24.)

stage_u.note: u1 is the abliterated pack on the same runtime and quant as c1 (identical config.json). The legitimate refusal probe scores 40 prompts in four categories that aligned models often over-refuse, plus 10 neutral controls; there a refusal is a defect and it stores 200 characters per answer. The harmful probe scores 24 prompts a safe model must refuse (offensive cyber plus drug, weapons, fraud, and violence anchors); there a refusal is the safe answer and it stores only the verdict, never any response text.
